content.title: About
content.content: White commercial bread is a bakery product made from high‑grade wheat flour, water, yeast, salt and sometimes a small amount of sugar and fats. It is produced on a large scale for retail chains and food service, featuring a soft crumb, light crust and neutral flavor, making it a versatile base for sandwiches, toast and open‑face meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first industrial bread was baked in the early 19th century after the invention of the steam oven.
White bread is often used in culinary schools as a “neutral” product for teaching mixing and shaping techniques.
In the United States more than 30 % of all baked goods sold are white commercial bread.
Gluten content in white bread is higher than in whole‑grain varieties because refined wheat flour is used.
Traditionally white bread was stored in ventilated bread boxes to prevent mold growth.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Bread provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fermentation by yeast produces thiamine, niacin and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: A modest amount of dietary fiber in white bread helps regulate bowel movements.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Its neutral taste allows a wide range of toppings, enhancing the nutritional value of meals.

items.title: Fortified versions
items.content: In many countries white bread is enriched with iron and folic acid to help prevent deficiencies.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, which may be undesirable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Regular consumption without adding whole‑grain foods may contribute to constipation.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some commercial loaves may contain preservatives, emulsifiers and flavor enhancers.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: A small percentage of the population may experience allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread can be eaten fresh, toasted, used for sandwiches, as a base for croutons, breadcrumbs in meat mixtures or for coating. It pairs well with butter, cheese, cold cuts, vegetables and spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bread in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag – it will keep flavor and texture for up to 3 months. Avoid keeping it in non‑ventilated plastic, which can promote mold growth.
